questions.q: Why does Castlebridge Logistics need to build a custom connector for its dispatch system?
options: Because Power Automate requires every flow to use at least one custom connector
Because the dispatch system is an internal API with no prebuilt connector in the Power Automate gallery
Because custom connectors run faster than gallery connectors
Because child flows cannot call gallery connectors
questions.explain: A custom connector exists to wrap an API that has no prebuilt connector. Castlebridge's dispatch system is homegrown, so nobody has built that wrapper for them.

questions.q: In the custom connector wizard, which section sets the authentication type an API expects?
options: General
Security
Definition
Test
questions.explain: The Security section is where you choose the authentication type — such as API Key, OAuth 2.0, or Basic — and configure its parameters.

questions.q: What does "Import from sample" actually do on the Definition tab?
options: It copies an existing connector's entire definition into the new connector
It builds the action's request and response parameters automatically from a real example you paste in
It imports sample flows that use the connector
It generates fake test data for the Test tab
questions.explain: Import from sample reads a real request and response you provide and turns its fields into named, typed parameters, instead of requiring you to hand-write a schema.

questions.q: Why does Castlebridge test the connector on the Test tab before using it in any flow?
options: Testing is required to publish the connector to the public gallery
It confirms the connection and authentication actually work against the real API, not just a schema that looks correct
The Test tab is the only place a connection can be created
Testing automatically fixes any authentication errors
questions.explain: A connector's definition can look valid and still fail against the real API. Running a real test call with a real connection confirms it actually works before any flow depends on it.

questions.q: Once Castlebridge's custom connector passes its test, how does it behave inside the flow designer?
options: It only works in flows created by the same person who built the connector
It appears and behaves like any built-in gallery connector, with typed inputs and outputs
It must be re-imported into every new flow that wants to use it
It can only be used with the Code section enabled
questions.explain: Once built and tested, a custom connector is searchable and usable in the designer exactly like a Microsoft-built connector, with the same typed action inputs and outputs.
